questions.stem: According to the passage, how much did Mary Kay pay for the legal rights to the skin care products that became the basis of her company?
questions.evidence: She paid $500 for the legal rights to the products.
questions.explanation_ko: 그는 제품에 대한 법적 권리를 500달러에 구입했다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as a prize Mary Kay Cosmetics offered top sales representatives?
options: Free college tuition for their children
questions.evidence: Prizes for high sales marks included special paid holidays and jewelry. Until a few years ago, a pink Cadillac was a top prize.
questions.explanation_ko: 유급 휴가, 보석, 핑크색 캐딜락은 언급되지만 자녀 대학 등록금 지원은 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the fact that representatives who recruited new saleswomen received part of their earnings?
options: The earnings-sharing system discouraged experienced representatives from recruiting new members.
The earnings-sharing system gave experienced representatives a financial incentive to recruit and train new saleswomen.
New representatives received no support from experienced ones.
Only the company's founder profited from new representatives joining.
questions.evidence: That way, experienced sales representatives would be willing to train new ones.
questions.explanation_ko: 신규 영업사원을 데려온 대표가 그 사람의 수익 일부를 받도록 한 것에서, 경험 많은 대표들이 신입을 적극적으로 모집·교육하도록 하는 금전적 동기를 만들었음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that Mary Kay started a foundation to fund cancer research after her third husband died of the disease?
options: To show how a personal loss led her to a new philanthropic goal
To argue that cosmetics companies should not engage in charity
To explain the history of cancer research funding in general
To criticize her husband's medical treatment
questions.evidence: After her third husband, Mel Ash, died of cancer in 1980, she wanted to help find a cure for the disease.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 설명은 개인적인 상실이 그를 새로운 자선 활동 목표로 이끌었음을 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "direct sellers" mean in "one of the most successful direct sellers of skin care products in America"?
options: companies that sell products through large retail stores only
companies that sell products straight to customers rather than through stores
companies that only sell products online
companies that manufacture but do not sell products
questions.evidence: Mary Kay Cosmetics became one of the most successful direct sellers of skin care products in America.
questions.explanation_ko: direct sellers는 매장을 거치지 않고 소비자에게 직접 판매하는 회사를 뜻합니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 어린 시절 대부분, 그는 아픈 아버지를 돌보았고 어머니는 식당에서 오랜 시간 일했다.
메리 케이는 자기 자신과 경쟁하는 것이 최선이라는 생각을 바탕으로 매출을 늘리고자 했다.
그는 1996년 뇌졸중을 겪을 때까지 사업체에서 계속 일했다.
영업 대표들은 메리 케이가 여성들이 돈을 벌면서도 가족과 시간을 보낼 수 있는 방법을 만들었다고 말한다.

key_points: Mary Kay Ash founded Mary Kay Cosmetics in Dallas in 1963 with a $500 investment in skin care product rights, after working to support her children as a single mother.
The company sold products through home demonstrations by independent sales representatives, and by 1965 it was already selling nearly a million dollars worth of products.

Mary Kay's system rewarded representatives with a share of earnings from saleswomen they recruited, encouraging experienced sellers to train newcomers, alongside prizes like paid holidays, jewelry, and a pink Cadillac.
After her third husband died of cancer, Mary Kay started a foundation supporting cancer research affecting women, which later expanded to also address violence against women.
main_idea: Mary Kay Ash built a small $500 investment into one of America's most successful direct-selling cosmetics companies, creating a system that rewarded sales representatives and later funded charitable causes.
restate_sentence: The idea was to sell skin care products through demonstrations in homes and offices.
